title: Halal Finder listing
description: Schema for a single Halal Finder place listing. Both listings.json (production placeholder, intentionally empty until sourced records exist) and sample-listings.json (fictional demo records) are JSON arrays of objects conforming to this schema; validate each array item against it. Core fields are required; additional display/extension attributes are permitted (additionalProperties: true) so the static MVP can carry UI-compatible fields (e.g. cuisine, price, emoji, art, desc, isSample) that a later database phase may promote, rename or drop. Required core fields match AGENTS.md and the Halal Finder strategy pack; evidence.status uses exactly the five sanctioned evidence statuses — never a generic 'verified' value.

id.description: Stable record identifier. Integers (minimum 1) are retained for the legacy fictional demo records; production records should use a non-empty string such as an internal UUID, database id or slug.

slug.description: Kebab-case, URL-safe identifier. Lowercase ASCII letters, digits and single hyphens only; no leading, trailing or doubled hyphens.

name.description: Public business name as shown to users.

type.description: Business category. Exactly these three values are supported in the MVP.

city.description: Town or city as displayed to users (e.g. 'London'). Keep separate from country; UIs may join the two with ', '.

country.description: Country as displayed to users (e.g. 'United Kingdom'). Keep casing consistent within a dataset. ISO 3166-1 codes may be adopted in a later schema revision.

address.description: Street address. Optional and never invented; omit when not reliably sourced.

sourceName.description: Human-readable name of the data source for this record (e.g. 'Written permission from business owner, 2026-09-01', 'Oldham Council open data (OGL v3)'). Fictional sample records use 'Halal Finder fictional sample dataset'. Always recorded so incorrect records can be traced, corrected or removed.

dataLicence.description: Licence under which this record may be used and republished (e.g. 'OGL v3.0', 'ODbL 1.0', 'Used with written permission', 'Unlicensed (fictional sample)'). Check before importing; record the licence name, not just a verdict.

fictional.description: true for demo/sample records that are not real businesses and carry no real halal evidence. Production records sourced from a real place must use false. Never set false for an unsourced or invented record.

isSample.description: Optional belt-and-braces marker used by sample-listings.json. true marks a record as demo/sample content that must never be presented as a real, verified listing.

isSponsored.description: true if this is a paid/promoted placement. Sponsorship never changes evidence status; sponsored records must be visibly labelled 'Sponsored' in any UI that renders them.

featured.description: UI-only 'example promotion' placement flag from the MVP. Not an endorsement and not an evidence signal.

cuisine.description: Display string for cuisine/category tags (e.g. 'Lebanese · Grill'). Free text; not a controlled vocabulary yet.

price.description: Currency-neutral price marker as shown in the MVP (e.g. '£', '££', '$', '¥¥', '$$', '₩₩', '€€'). One to four identical currency symbols; not a real price quote.

emoji.description: Illustrative emoji art for the demo card header. UI must render it aria-hidden; never a functional icon.

art.description: Optional gradient art class for the demo card header (illustrative only until real photography exists). One of: green, blue, purple. Omit when the demo used no art.

desc.description: Short display description copy. Field name kept compatible with the MVP UI (desc).

tags.description: Optional display tags. Fictional sample records carry ['Sample data', 'Not a real verification'] so any consumer renders the fiction labelling.

coordinates.description: Optional WGS84 coordinates. Never invented — omit entirely when not reliably sourced. lat in [-90, 90], lng in [-180, 180].

demoStatusLabel.description: Sample-only extension preserving the exact legacy MVP badge copy (e.g. 'Certification evidence example'). Do not use in production records; production UIs derive labels from evidence.status.

evidence.description: Evidence object. Required; every listing must carry exactly one of the five evidence statuses. Only status is required; all other fields are optional and must be omitted (never invented) when unknown.

status.description: The five sanctioned evidence statuses. certificate_reviewed requires an actual reviewed third-party certificate; business_declared is an unconfirmed business claim; community_reported is a user report awaiting review; muslim_friendly is context, not proof; not_verified means evidence is missing, unclear, expired or unconfirmed. Never a generic 'verified'.

issuer.description: Certifier/issuer name where relevant (e.g. the certifying body). Shown only as permitted by the source.

certificateId.description: Certificate identifier where appropriate and where publication is permitted. Never exposed if the issuer or business has not consented.

scope.description: What the evidence actually covers, e.g. 'Premises and all menu items', 'Specific products only', 'Halal chicken only'. A certificate for one branch, product or supplier must not be generalised.

expiryDate.description: Certificate expiry date, ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD. A certificate_reviewed record whose expiryDate is in the past must be treated as downgraded to not_verified until re-reviewed (see tests/unit/evidence-status.test.cjs).

lastCheckedAt.description: Date the evidence was last checked/reviewed, ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD. Detail views must show this date, or state that evidence is unconfirmed when absent.

nextReviewDate.description: Scheduled next review date, ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD.

sourceUrl.description: URL of the evidence source or licence reference (http/https only).

sourceLicence.description: Licence of the evidence source itself (e.g. 'OGL v3.0', 'ODbL 1.0', 'Used with written permission', 'Unlicensed (fictional sample)').

reviewerRole.description: Role of the reviewer, never a personal identity (e.g. 'Evidence reviewer', 'Moderator'). Personal identity lives only in access-restricted internal audit logs.

limitations.description: User-visible limitation notes explaining what was not checked or does not apply (e.g. 'Halal chicken only', 'Menu items marked halal only'). Keep wording plain; never soften into false confidence.
